contents.html: The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of non-national security-related information in Federal information systems. This Interagency Report discusses ITL’s research, guidelines, and outreach efforts in information system security, and its collaborative activities with industry, government, and academic organizations.
contents.html_ja: 国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の情報技術研究所（ITL）は、国の計測・標準の基盤に技術面でリーダーシップを発揮することにより、米国の経済と公共の福祉を促進しています。ITL は、情報技術の発展と生産的な利用を進めるために、試験、試験方法、参照データ、概念実証の実装、技術分析を開発しています。ITL の責務には、連邦情報システムにおける、国家安全保障に関係しない情報について、費用対効果の高いセキュリティとプライバシーを確保するための、管理面、運営面、技術面、物理面の標準およびガイドラインの策定が含まれます。この省庁間報告書は、ITL の情報システムセキュリティに関する研究、ガイドライン、アウトリーチ活動と、産業界、政府、学術機関との協働活動について論じます。

contents.html: On August 27, 2004, the President signed Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) [1], entitled “Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors.” HSPD-12 required the development and implementation of a government-wide standard for secure and reliable forms of identification for Federal employees and contractors. In response, NIST developed the Federal Information Processing Standard 201 (FIPS 201) [2], Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors, to establish a standard for identity credentials. NIST also issued several special publications in support of FIPS 201 to enable interoperable implementations.
contents.html_ja: 2004 年 8 月 27 日、大統領は、「Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors」と題する国土安全保障大統領指令 12（HSPD-12）[1] に署名しました。HSPD-12 は、連邦職員および契約業者のための、安全で信頼できる身分証明の形式に関する、政府全体の標準の策定と実装を求めました。これを受けて NIST は、身元証明書の標準を確立するために、連邦情報処理標準 201（FIPS 201）[2]『Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors』を策定しました。NIST はまた、相互運用可能な実装を可能にするために、FIPS 201 を支援するいくつかの特別刊行物を発行しました。

contents.html: FIPS 201 and its associated special publications define a method to perform biometric match-off-card authentication of a PIV cardholder when the PIV card is inserted into a contact smart card reader. Today, many smart cards, however, implement match-on-card technologies and are desiged to perform cardholder authentication using contactless interface. Contactless match-on-card operation requires additional security measures to ensure the transaction data is encrypted and can be securely transmitted, which can impact performance. NIST conducted the Secure Biometric Match-on-Card (SBMOC) feasibility study to understand the effects of security on performance. This report describes the tests that were conducted to obtain timing metrics for the SBMOC feasibility study and provides a summary of the test results.
contents.html_ja: FIPS 201 とその関連する特別刊行物は、PIVカードが接触型スマートカードリーダーに挿入されたときに、PIVカード保持者の生体カード外照合認証を行う方法を定めています。しかし現在では、多くのスマートカードがカード内照合技術を実装しており、非接触インターフェースを用いてカード保持者の認証を行うように設計されています。非接触のカード内照合の動作では、トランザクションデータが暗号化され、安全に送信できることを確保するための追加のセキュリティ対策が必要であり、これが性能に影響を与える可能性があります。NIST は、セキュリティが性能に及ぼす影響を理解するために、セキュアな生体照合カード内照合（SBMOC）の実現可能性調査を実施しました。この報告書は、SBMOC の実現可能性調査のために時間メトリクスを得る目的で実施した試験について説明し、試験結果の要約を示します。

contents.html: In June 2007, NIST extended an open invitation to companies to participate in the SBMOC feasibility study. The purpose of the study was to determine if secure biometric match-on-card operations could be performed in less than 2.5 seconds per transaction.<sup>1</sup> The feasibility study was conducted per guidelines set forth in the NIST Test Approach for SBMOC Feasibility Study (see Appendix D). The test approach describes a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) based protocol for performing secure biometric match-on-card authentication of a cardholder using contactless operation. The protocol describes general message transactions so that variations in protocol implementation by participants are acceptable so long as the security, functional, and performance objectives defined in Sections 2 and 3 of Appendix D are met. contents.html_ja: 2007 年 6 月、NIST は、SBMOC の実現可能性調査への参加を企業に広く呼びかけました。この調査の目的は、セキュアな生体照合カード内照合の操作を、1 トランザクションあたり 2.5 秒未満で実行できるかどうかを判断することでした。<sup>1</sup> 実現可能性調査は、NIST Test Approach for SBMOC Feasibility Study（付録 D を参照）に定めるガイドラインに従って実施されました。この試験アプローチは、非接触操作を用いてカード保持者のセキュアな生体照合カード内照合認証を行うための、公開鍵基盤（PKI）に基づくプロトコルを説明しています。このプロトコルは一般的なメッセージトランザクションを記述しているため、付録 D の第 2 節および第 3 節に定めるセキュリティ、機能、性能の目標が満たされる限り、参加者によるプロトコル実装の違いは許容されます。使用事例のシナリオの例は、次のとおりです。

contents.html: At the time this study began, NIST was unable to identify any commercial product meeting all of the requirements in Appendix D. Participants worked with NIST to understand the requirements and then developed submissions. Submissions received for the feasibility study that met the stated objectives were tested by NIST. The subsequent sections in this report discuss the test procedures and the results of successful tests obtained from the feasibility study. The results of unsuccessful tests are not reported.

contents.html: In order to obtain performance timing metrics, a test fixture was developed that implements the secure message protocol for each Device Under Test (DUT) and records the measured transaction times. Test cases executed for the feasibility study were designed to study how matching/non-matching templates, varying minutia counts, and different encryption algorithms impact transaction times. The following subsections describe the test fixture and procedures used for the feasibility study.
contents.html_ja: 性能の時間指標を得るために、各被試験デバイス（DUT）に対してセキュアメッセージプロトコルを実装し、測定したトランザクション時間を記録するテストフィクスチャを開発しました。実現可能性調査のために実行した試験ケースは、一致するテンプレートと一致しないテンプレート、マニューシャ数の違い、暗号アルゴリズムの違いが、トランザクション時間にどのように影響するかを調べるように設計されました。以下の小節では、実現可能性調査で用いたテストフィクスチャと手順を説明します。

contents.html: To perform time measurements, the test fixture sends Application Protocol Data Units (APDU) to a DUT using the SCardTransmit command. The time it takes to execute a SCardTransmit command, which is obtained by computing the time difference before and after a call to SCardTransmit, is then recorded to an output file. For APDUs that require multiple calls to SCardTransmit (e.g., GET RESPONSE), the total elapsed time is determined by adding the time to execute each SCardTransmit operation. An example message sequence between a DUT and the test fixture is as follows:
contents.html_ja: 時間測定を行うために、テストフィクスチャは SCardTransmit コマンドを用いて、DUT にアプリケーションプロトコルデータユニット（APDU）を送信します。SCardTransmit コマンドの実行にかかる時間は、SCardTransmit の呼び出しの前後の時間差を計算して得られ、出力ファイルに記録されます。SCardTransmit を複数回呼び出す必要がある APDU（たとえば GET RESPONSE）については、各 SCardTransmit 操作の実行時間を足し合わせて、経過時間の合計を求めます。DUT とテストフィクスチャの間のメッセージシーケンスの例は、次のとおりです。

contents.html: For each test case, a DUT was loaded with a reference fingerprint template containing a minutia count of 41, 34, or 27 in either ANSI 378 or ISO/IEC 19794-2 compact format (depending on the DUT being tested). In addition, each DUT was loaded with an X.509 certificate that was generated using the NIST PIV Data Generator tool. The size of the generated certificates was kept consistent by changing only the public key modulus and exponent associated with each certificate to match the public/private key pair stored on a DUT. For tests using Rivest Shamir Adleman (RSA) 1024, the size of the certificate used was 1,345 bytes and for RSA 2048, the certificate size was 1,477 bytes.
contents.html_ja: 各試験ケースでは、DUT に、ANSI 378 または ISO/IEC 19794-2 コンパクト形式（試験対象の DUT による）で、マニューシャ数が 41、34、または 27 の参照指紋テンプレートをロードしました。さらに、各 DUT には、NIST PIV Data Generator ツールを用いて生成した X.509 証明書をロードしました。生成した証明書のサイズは、各証明書に関連付けられた公開鍵の法（modulus）と指数だけを、DUT に格納された公開鍵・秘密鍵ペアに合うよう変更することにより、一定に保ちました。Rivest Shamir Adleman（RSA）1024 を用いる試験では、使用した証明書のサイズは 1,345 バイトであり、RSA 2048 では、証明書のサイズは 1,477 バイトでした。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p10: 画像と文字層で照合

contents.html: Testing consisted of sending matching and non-matching sample fingerprint templates to a DUT for verification in alternating sequence. First, sample fingerprint templates containing a minutia count of 41 were sent to the DUT for verification and time values were recorded. The process was repeated for sample fingerprint templates containing a minutia count of 34 and 27. Live fingerprint scans were not used in the tests since it was desirable to maintain a controlled test environment where the minutia count of the sample fingerprint templates could be regulated. Instead, the sample fingerprint templates were read from files generated from fingerprint scans beforehand. For each test case, 200 trials were run so that 100 time values could be collected each for matching and non-matching templates.
contents.html_ja: 試験では、照合するサンプル指紋テンプレートと照合しないサンプル指紋テンプレートを交互に DUT に送信して検証しました。まず、マニューシャ数が 41 のサンプル指紋テンプレートを DUT に送信して検証し、時間の値を記録しました。この過程を、マニューシャ数が 34 および 27 のサンプル指紋テンプレートについても繰り返しました。サンプル指紋テンプレートのマニューシャ数を調整できる管理された試験環境を維持することが望ましかったため、試験ではライブの指紋スキャンを使用しませんでした。代わりに、サンプル指紋テンプレートは、事前に指紋スキャンから生成したファイルから読み込みました。各試験ケースについて 200 回の試行を実施し、照合テンプレートと非照合テンプレートについて、それぞれ 100 個の時間の値を収集しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p10: 画像と文字層で照合

contents.html: The DUT was powered continuously during the automated sequence of 200 trials. As a consequence, transaction delays that could result from operations at DUT power-up, for example FIPS 140-2 power-up diagnostic tests, are not visible in the measurements.
contents.html_ja: DUT は、200 回の試行の自動シーケンスの間、継続的に給電されていました。その結果、たとえば FIPS 140-2 の電源投入時診断テストなど、DUT の電源投入時の動作によって生じる可能性のあるトランザクションの遅延は、測定値には現れません。

contents.html: Timing metrics obtained with the test fixture could not be validated with a protocol analyzer since one could not be acquired within the SBMOC test framework that supports the high-speed data rates used by the SCM SDI010 reader. However, the test fixure was built on a test framework for a previous NIST study in which timing metrics were obtained and validated with a protocol analyzer. Hence, there is a reasonable degree of confidence that the timing metrics reported in this document are accurate.

contents.html: Appendix B contains graphs of the response times for each DUT, separated by matching and non-matching results as well as minutia count. A 17 ms fluctuation is visible in the response time charts, e.g., in Figure C-1. This fluctuation can be attributed to the Windows NT clock resolution of the host PC, which is 1/60 second or 17 ms. Such fluctuations are recorded whenever a fixed duration phenomenon is measured repeatedly, starting at random points with respect to a clock tick. Assuming the DUT response time is fixed, the actual DUT response time is approximately the computed average response time, as reported in Appendix A. Whether the assumption holds or not, a 17 ms fluctuation is less than 3% of the measured values in all cases.
contents.html_ja: 付録 B には、各 DUT の応答時間のグラフを、照合結果と非照合結果、およびマニューシャ数ごとに分けて示しています。応答時間のチャート（たとえば図 C-1）には、17 ms の変動が見られます。この変動は、ホスト PC の Windows NT のクロック分解能が 1/60 秒、すなわち 17 ms であることに起因すると考えられます。このような変動は、クロックのティックに対してランダムな時点から開始して、一定の長さの現象を繰り返し測定するときには、常に記録されます。DUT の応答時間が一定であると仮定すると、実際の DUT の応答時間は、付録 A で報告している、計算された平均応答時間にほぼ等しくなります。この仮定が成り立つかどうかにかかわらず、17 ms の変動は、いずれの場合も測定値の 3% 未満です。

contents.html: The timing metrics obtained from the SBMOC feasibility study showed that it is possible to securely perform biometric match-on-card operations over the contactless interface of a smart card within 2.5 seconds, while meeting the constraints in Appendix D except the accuracy constraint. The study also showed that the amount of time required to complete an SBMOC operation is dependent on a number of factors, such as the cryptographic mechanisms used, the minutia count of the reference and sample fingerprint templates, and the format of the fingerprint templates.
contents.html_ja: SBMOC の実現可能性調査で得られた時間メトリクスは、精度の制約を除き、付録 D の制約を満たしながら、スマートカードの非接触インターフェースを介して生体照合カード内照合を 2.5 秒以内に安全に実行できることを示しました。この調査はまた、SBMOC の動作の完了に必要な時間が、使用する暗号方式、参照用およびサンプル指紋テンプレートのマニューシャ数、指紋テンプレートの形式など、多くの要因に依存することも示しました。

contents.html: Accuracy testing of ISO/IEC 19794-2 devices is in progress at this time. Partial results indicate that some devices exhibit accuracy approaching that measured for Minutiae Interoperability Exchange Test (MINEX) 04 implementations, and are likely to exceed the PIV accuracy requirements in Special Publication (SP) 800-76-1. Results will be announced at http://fingerprint.nist.gov/minexII/.
contents.html_ja: ISO/IEC 19794-2 デバイスの精度試験は、現在進行中です。部分的な結果は、一部のデバイスが、Minutiae Interoperability Exchange Test（MINEX）04 の実装で測定された精度に近い精度を示し、特別刊行物（SP）800-76-1 の PIV の精度要件を上回る可能性が高いことを示しています。結果は http://fingerprint.nist.gov/minexII/ で発表されます。

contents.html: The feasibility study participants informed us that some of the DUTs were constructed by adding firmware and data to PIV card stock that had passed NIST NPIVP and FIPS 140-2 testing. These remarks are further evidence that SBMOC is technically feasible through firmware extensions to existing smart cards.
contents.html_ja: 実現可能性調査の参加者によると、一部の DUT は、NIST NPIVP と FIPS 140-2 の試験に合格した PIVカードのカード素材にファームウェアとデータを追加して構築されたとのことです。これらの発言は、既存のスマートカードのファームウェア拡張によって SBMOC が技術的に実現可能であることを示すさらなる証拠です。

contents.html_ja: D.1 目的
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本: 節見出し

contents.html: FIPS 201-1 and associated NIST Special Publications define a method to perform biometric authentication of a PIV cardholder when the PIV Card is inserted into a contact smart card reader. In some use cases, however, contactless operation is required. Security concerns have hindered communication of biometric data transfer over the contactless interface. The transaction data can be protected by secure messaging and data encryption, but these methods can impact performance. To understand the effects of security on performance, NIST will conduct a technical feasibility study of secure data transfer over the contactless interface to perform Secure Biometric Match-On-Card (SBMOC) operations. Eventually, NIST may propose an extension of the FIPS 201 standard that achieves secure biometric authentication in the contactless mode of operation, but such a proposal is not an immediate goal of this study.
contents.html_ja: FIPS 201-1 と関連する NIST 特別刊行物は、PIVカードが接触型スマートカードリーダーに挿入されたときに、PIVカード保持者の生体認証を行う方法を定めています。しかし、ユースケースによっては、非接触の動作が求められます。セキュリティ上の懸念により、非接触インターフェースを介した生体データの転送が妨げられてきました。トランザクションデータはセキュアメッセージングとデータの暗号化によって保護できますが、これらの方法は性能に影響を与える可能性があります。セキュリティが性能に及ぼす影響を理解するために、NIST は、非接触インターフェースを介したセキュアなデータ転送によってセキュア生体照合カード内照合（SBMOC）の動作を行う技術的実現可能性調査を実施します。NIST は最終的に、非接触の動作モードでセキュアな生体認証を実現する FIPS 201 標準の拡張を提案する可能性がありますが、そのような提案はこの調査の当面の目標ではありません。

contents.html: The study will use PKI to create an authenticated, secure session (like an SSL/TLS session) that protects the integrity and confidentiality of messages sent from the terminal to a smart card, and the integrity and authenticity of messages sent from the smart card to the terminal. The protocol never releases biometric data from the smart card, called the Device Under Test (DUT) in this document. Instead, the DUT receives an encrypted sample template from a biometric reader, performs a match against a reference template stored on the DUT, and returns a logically signed Yes/No result to the reader.
contents.html_ja: この調査では、PKI を用いて、端末からスマートカードに送られるメッセージの完全性と機密性、およびスマートカードから端末に送られるメッセージの完全性と真正性を保護する、認証されたセキュアなセッション（SSL/TLS セッションのようなもの）を作成します。このプロトコルは、この文書で被試験デバイス（DUT）と呼ぶスマートカードから、生体データを一切外部に出しません。代わりに、DUT は生体リーダーから暗号化されたサンプルテンプレートを受け取り、DUT に格納された参照テンプレートと照合し、論理的に署名された Yes/No の結果をリーダーに返します。

contents.html: Preliminary tests of BMOC operation have shown that a BMOC operation for physical access could be performed within 500 milliseconds without secure messaging. Tests of PKI transaction times suggest that the approach could meet a success criterion of less than 2.5 seconds per transaction.
contents.html_ja: BMOC の動作の予備試験では、物理アクセスのための BMOC の動作を、セキュアメッセージングなしで 500 ミリ秒以内に実行できることが示されました。PKI のトランザクション時間の試験は、このアプローチが 1 トランザクションあたり 2.5 秒未満という成功基準を満たしうることを示唆しています。

contents.html_ja: D.2 セキュリティの目標
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本: 節見出し

contents.html: FIPS 201-1 permits biometric data to be released only across the contact interface of a PIV Card, and only after activation of the PIV Card through presentation of the cardholder’s Personal Identification Number (PIN). These restrictions achieve two security objectives: communication of biometric data occurs only over a trusted communication channel that is not easily subject to eavesdropping attacks (namely, the wired contacts inside the smart card reader); and the PIV cardholder implicitly attests to the legitimacy of the smart card reader, as they indicate by entering the PIN on the smart card reader keypad. FIPS 201-1 enables biometric authentication to occur without imposing a technical requirement for automatic authentication of smart card readers to PIV Cards. Such a requirement, it was believed, would add unacceptable key management costs. (The PIV fingerprint object is digitally signed, and the signature can be used to verify authenticity and integrity of the data.) This feasibility study will evaluate the impact of a secure protocol on transaction performance, when the protocol meets these security objectives:
contents.html_ja: FIPS 201-1 は、生体データの送出を、PIVカードの接触インターフェースを介する場合に限り、かつ、カード保持者の個人識別番号（PIN）の提示によって PIVカードを有効化した後に限り、許可しています。これらの制限により、2 つのセキュリティ目標が達成されます。1 つは、生体データの通信が、盗聴攻撃の影響を受けにくい信頼できる通信チャネル（すなわち、スマートカードリーダー内部の有線接点）でのみ行われることです。もう 1 つは、カード保持者がスマートカードリーダーのキーパッドに PIN を入力することによって、そのリーダーが正当であると暗黙のうちに表明することです。FIPS 201-1 は、スマートカードリーダーから PIVカードへの自動認証に関する技術的要件を課すことなく、生体認証を可能にしています。そのような要件は、許容できない鍵管理コストを伴うと考えられたためです。（PIV 指紋オブジェクトにはデジタル署名が付されており、その署名を用いてデータの真正性と完全性を検証できます。）この実現可能性調査では、次のセキュリティ目標を満たすセキュアなプロトコルが、トランザクションの性能に及ぼす影響を評価します。

contents.html: The performance tests will measure the duration of phases during the SBMOC transaction. The rationale for the approach relies on two observations. First, the PIV System trust model is founded on PKI, and by design, any PIV Card can authenticate itself to another system element at a medium high assurance level using a private key and certificate stored on the card. Second, if a biometric match operation is performed on the PIV Card using SBMOC technology, there is no need to release biometric data from the PIV Card to any other system element (thus satisfying SO3 in Section D.2).
contents.html_ja: 性能試験では、SBMOC トランザクションの間の各フェーズの所要時間を測定します。このアプローチの根拠は、2 つの観察に基づいています。第 1 に、PIV システムの信頼モデルは PKI を基盤としており、設計上、どの PIVカードも、カードに格納された秘密鍵と証明書を用いて、システムの別の要素に対し、中程度に高い保証レベルで自分自身を認証できます。第 2 に、SBMOC 技術を用いて PIVカード上で生体照合を行えば、生体データを PIVカードからシステムの他の要素に送出する必要がありません（したがって、第 D.2 節の SO3 を満たします）。

contents.html: In outline, the use scenario is as follows. The cardholder presents their card to a contactless biometric reader, and presents their finger to the biometric scanner. The scanner obtains a fingerprint image which is transformed into the sample template, encrypted, and transmitted via contactless into the PIV Card. The PIV Card decrypts the template, matches the sample template against the reference template stored on the PIV Card, and returns a signed “Yes” or “No” result to the smart card reader.

In June 2007, NIST extended an open invitation to companies to participate in the SBMOC feasibility study. The purpose of the study was to determine if secure biometric match-on-card operations could be performed in less than 2.5 seconds per transaction.1 The feasibility study was conducted per guidelines set forth in the NIST Test Approach for SBMOC Feasibility Study (see Appendix D). The test approach describes a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) based protocol for performing secure biometric match-on-card authentication of a cardholder using contactless operation. The protocol describes general message transactions so that variations in protocol implementation by participants are acceptable so long as the security, functional, and performance objectives defined in Sections 2 and 3 of Appendix D are met. An example use case scenario is as follows:
+ The cardholder presents their card to a contactless biometric reader.
+ The cardholder presents their finger to the biometric scanner.
+ The host establishes a secure session with the card.
+ The host prepares an encrypted template containing the fingerprint (image or minutia) and transmits it via contactless interface to the card.
+ The card decrypts the template and compares it with the reference template stored on the card.
+ The card returns signed result (i.e., Yes/No) to the host.
1 The template generation time (which is live presentation of a fingerprint) is excluded from the time measurement.
3.1 Test Fixture
+ Average2 time to establish a secure session
+ Average time to transmit the encrypted biometric data to the DUT and receive a match result
+ Average total time to perform a complete biometric match-on-card transaction
The test fixture selects the SBMOC application on the card.
The test fixture performs Get Data to read the PKI certificate from the DUT and validates the certificate.
The test fixture requests a challenge from the DUT. The DUT responds with a challenge.
The text fixture and DUT generate encryption and Message Authentication Code (MAC) session keys, and finish establishing a secure session.
The text fixture encrypts biometric data using session key and sends it to the DUT for verification. The DUT responds with the signed match / no-match result.
2 Throughout this report, “average” is the arithmetic mean of the measured values.

1. Introduction

On August 27, 2004, the President signed Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) [1], entitled “Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors.” HSPD-12 required the development and implementation of a government-wide standard for secure and reliable forms of identification for Federal employees and contractors. In response, NIST developed the Federal Information Processing Standard 201 (FIPS 201) [2], Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors, to establish a standard for identity credentials. NIST also issued several special publications in support of FIPS 201 to enable interoperable implementations.

FIPS 201 and its associated special publications define a method to perform biometric match-off-card authentication of a PIV cardholder when the PIV card is inserted into a contact smart card reader. Today, many smart cards, however, implement match-on-card technologies and are desiged to perform cardholder authentication using contactless interface. Contactless match-on-card operation requires additional security measures to ensure the transaction data is encrypted and can be securely transmitted, which can impact performance. NIST conducted the Secure Biometric Match-on-Card (SBMOC) feasibility study to understand the effects of security on performance. This report describes the tests that were conducted to obtain timing metrics for the SBMOC feasibility study and provides a summary of the test results.
This feasibility study also allows NIST to explore smart card technology advancements for possible extension of the FIPS 201 and / or other smart card standards.
2. Background

At the time this study began, NIST was unable to identify any commercial product meeting all of the requirements in Appendix D. Participants worked with NIST to understand the requirements and then developed submissions. Submissions received for the feasibility study that met the stated objectives were tested by NIST. The subsequent sections in this report discuss the test procedures and the results of successful tests obtained from the feasibility study. The results of unsuccessful tests are not reported.
3. Test Process

In order to obtain performance timing metrics, a test fixture was developed that implements the secure message protocol for each Device Under Test (DUT) and records the measured transaction times. Test cases executed for the feasibility study were designed to study how matching/non-matching templates, varying minutia counts, and different encryption algorithms impact transaction times. The following subsections describe the test fixture and procedures used for the feasibility study.

The test fixture uses the Win32 Smart Card Application Programming Interface (API) library to communicate with DUTs and smart card readers. The library was used to acquire the following time measurements:

To perform time measurements, the test fixture sends Application Protocol Data Units (APDU) to a DUT using the SCardTransmit command. The time it takes to execute a SCardTransmit command, which is obtained by computing the time difference before and after a call to SCardTransmit, is then recorded to an output file. For APDUs that require multiple calls to SCardTransmit (e.g., GET RESPONSE), the total elapsed time is determined by adding the time to execute each SCardTransmit operation. The smart card reader used in the tests was an SCM SDI010 dual interface reader. The reader’s technical specifications are given in Table 2.
Table 2. Smart Card Reader Technical Specifications

For each test case, a DUT was loaded with a reference fingerprint template containing a minutia count of 41, 34, or 27 in either ANSI 378 or ISO/IEC 19794-2 compact format (depending on the DUT being tested). In addition, each DUT was loaded with an X.509 certificate that was generated using the NIST PIV Data Generator tool. The size of the generated certificates was kept consistent by changing only the public key modulus and exponent associated with each certificate to match the public/private key pair stored on a DUT. For tests using Rivest Shamir Adleman (RSA) 1024, the size of the certificate used was 1,345 bytes and for RSA 2048, the certificate size was 1,477 bytes.

Testing consisted of sending matching and non-matching sample fingerprint templates to a DUT for verification in alternating sequence. First, sample fingerprint templates containing a minutia count of 41 were sent to the DUT for verification and time values were recorded. The process was repeated for sample fingerprint templates containing a minutia count of 34 and 27. Live fingerprint scans were not used in the tests since it was desirable to maintain a controlled test environment where the minutia count of the sample fingerprint templates could be regulated. Instead, the sample fingerprint templates were read from files generated from fingerprint scans beforehand. For each test case, 200 trials were run so that 100 time values could be collected each for matching and non-matching templates.

The DUT was powered continuously during the automated sequence of 200 trials. As a consequence, transaction delays that could result from operations at DUT power-up, for example FIPS 140-2 power-up diagnostic tests, are not visible in the measurements.

4. Results

Timing metrics obtained with the test fixture could not be validated with a protocol analyzer since one could not be acquired within the SBMOC test framework that supports the high-speed data rates used by the SCM SDI010 reader. However, the test fixure was built on a test framework for a previous NIST study in which timing metrics were obtained and validated with a protocol analyzer. Hence, there is a reasonable degree of confidence that the timing metrics reported in this document are accurate.

Appendix B contains graphs of the response times for each DUT, separated by matching and non-matching results as well as minutia count. A 17 ms fluctuation is visible in the response time charts, e.g., in Figure C-1. This fluctuation can be attributed to the Windows NT clock resolution of the host PC, which is 1/60 second or 17 ms. Such fluctuations are recorded whenever a fixed duration phenomenon is measured repeatedly, starting at random points with respect to a clock tick. Assuming the DUT response time is fixed, the actual DUT response time is approximately the computed average response time, as reported in Appendix A. Whether the assumption holds or not, a 17 ms fluctuation is less than 3% of the measured values in all cases.

5. Conclusion

The timing metrics obtained from the SBMOC feasibility study showed that it is possible to securely perform biometric match-on-card operations over the contactless interface of a smart card within 2.5 seconds, while meeting the constraints in Appendix D except the accuracy constraint. The study also showed that the amount of time required to complete an SBMOC operation is dependent on a number of factors, such as the cryptographic mechanisms used, the minutia count of the reference and sample fingerprint templates, and the format of the fingerprint templates.

The feasibility study participants informed us that some of the DUTs were constructed by adding firmware and data to PIV card stock that had passed NIST NPIVP and FIPS 140-2 testing. These remarks are further evidence that SBMOC is technically feasible through firmware extensions to existing smart cards.

FIPS 201-1 and associated NIST Special Publications define a method to perform biometric authentication of a PIV cardholder when the PIV Card is inserted into a contact smart card reader. In some use cases, however, contactless operation is required. Security concerns have hindered communication of biometric data transfer over the contactless interface. The transaction data can be protected by secure messaging and data encryption, but these methods can impact performance. To understand the effects of security on performance, NIST will conduct a technical feasibility study of secure data transfer over the contactless interface to perform Secure Biometric Match-On-Card (SBMOC) operations. Eventually, NIST may propose an extension of the FIPS 201 standard that achieves secure biometric authentication in the contactless mode of operation, but such a proposal is not an immediate goal of this study.

The study will use PKI to create an authenticated, secure session (like an SSL/TLS session) that protects the integrity and confidentiality of messages sent from the terminal to a smart card, and the integrity and authenticity of messages sent from the smart card to the terminal. The protocol never releases biometric data from the smart card, called the Device Under Test (DUT) in this document. Instead, the DUT receives an encrypted sample template from a biometric reader, performs a match against a reference template stored on the DUT, and returns a logically signed Yes/No result to the reader.

Preliminary tests of BMOC operation have shown that a BMOC operation for physical access could be performed within 500 milliseconds without secure messaging. Tests of PKI transaction times suggest that the approach could meet a success criterion of less than 2.5 seconds per transaction.

FIPS 201-1 permits biometric data to be released only across the contact interface of a PIV Card, and only after activation of the PIV Card through presentation of the cardholder’s Personal Identification Number (PIN). These restrictions achieve two security objectives: communication of biometric data occurs only over a trusted communication channel that is not easily subject to eavesdropping attacks (namely, the wired contacts inside the smart card reader); and the PIV cardholder implicitly attests to the legitimacy of the smart card reader, as they indicate by entering the PIN on the smart card reader keypad. FIPS 201-1 enables biometric authentication to occur without imposing a technical requirement for automatic authentication of smart card readers to PIV Cards. Such a requirement, it was believed, would add unacceptable key management costs. (The PIV fingerprint object is digitally signed, and the signature can be used to verify authenticity and integrity of the data.) This feasibility study will evaluate the impact of a secure protocol on transaction performance, when the protocol meets these security objectives:

These security objectives are aligned with the high-level security objectives of FIPS 201-1. They protect both the integrity of the biometric authentication transaction and the privacy of the cardholder’s biometric data, while avoiding the potential cost of reader authentication key management.
The Device Under Test (DUT) shall be a smart card having ISO/IEC 7810 physical and mechanical characteristics.
The Device Under test shall be capable of contact (via ISO/IEC 7816-3 methods, consistent with NIST SP800-73-1) and contactless (via ISO/IEC 14443 methods, consistent with NIST SP800-73-1).

Preferably, the DUT is listed on the General Services Administration (GSA) HSPD-12 Approved Product List, and modified only by the addition of BMOC firmware. The DUT may also be a type of smart card not on the GSA Approved Product List (APL). In this case, NIST will determine if the DUT could host a PIV card-application at reasonable development cost, and if so, the DUT will be tested.

The DUT may not have an NPIVP or a Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) certificate. In this case, NIST will determine if the DUT could pass NPIVP and CMVP testing at reasonable development cost, and if so, the DUT will be tested.
The DUT should perform a Biometric Match-On-Card authentication transaction and meet the security objectives described in Section D.2.

The biometric matching algorithm on the DUT should demonstrate accuracy meeting the criteria of SP800-76-1 Section 8.10 by testing in either the NIST MINEX II or Ongoing MINEX activity. (Note: accuracy testing may run concurrently with performance and security testing.)

The fingerprint sample template sent from the reader to the DUT should be represented following either ISO 19794-2 finger minutiae card or ANSI 378 format. Any extensions or options must be fully documented in the submitted protocol documentation.
Both RSA 1024 and RSA 2048 should be available as asymmetric algorithm alternatives unless one of these is not available on the DUT.
AES (preferred), 3TDEA, or 2TDEA (deprecated) should be implemented at the symmetric encryption algorithm.

The target transaction time for the SBMOC Technical Feasibility Study is 2.5 seconds or less and is measured from steps 2 through 10 in Section D.5. Performance will be measured and reported separately for matching and non-matching cases.

Once a complete submission package has been received, NIST will begin a security analysis of the SBMOC protocol to determine if it meets the security-related objectives of Sections D.2 and D.3. NIST will construct the client-side protocol implementation in the test framework. NIST will develop a new client-side protocol implementation for each submitted DUT (this will insure that NIST is able to construct working client-side software from the protocol documentation).

The test fixture will record the duration of each command-response transaction between the host and the card. A test record will therefore contain a complete log of all APDUs exchanged, and timing on each request-response pair individually. A trial will run tests and reference templates, and with non-matching sample and reference templates, to highlight any differences in transaction time arising form the match result. If the reference template object contains multiple templates, trials will be designed to disclose the effects of multiple templates (e.g., separate trials matching first template vs. second on variance, break down communication and processing time per request-response cycle, document the amount of data transmitted (in both directions) during the protocol scenario, and estimate the command-response time per sub-activity (e.g., “read certificate, “general authenticate”, “verify”).

The performance tests will measure the duration of phases during the SBMOC transaction. The rationale for the approach relies on two observations. First, the PIV System trust model is founded on PKI, and by design, any PIV Card can authenticate itself to another system element at a medium high assurance level using a private key and certificate stored on the card. Second, if a biometric match operation is performed on the PIV Card using SBMOC technology, there is no need to release biometric data from the PIV Card to any other system element (thus satisfying SO3 in Section D.2).
Variations in protocol implementation are acceptable provided that the objectives in Sections D.2 and D.3 are achieved.

In outline, the use scenario is as follows. The cardholder presents their card to a contactless biometric reader, and presents their finger to the biometric scanner. The scanner obtains a fingerprint image which is transformed into the sample template, encrypted, and transmitted via contactless into the PIV Card. The PIV Card decrypts the template, matches the sample template against the reference template stored on the PIV Card, and returns a signed “Yes” or “No” result to the smart card reader.
